data: 1[いち]升[しょう] 瓶[びん]を 2[に]本[ほん]も 飲[の]んだの!?
Did you drink two one-shō bottles of sake!?
Counter,Somewhat Common
升 · しょう · Mochi, sake bottles, rice, sake, shochu, etc. A 升 indicates 1.8 liters, which is ten times more than 1合 (ごう).

遍 · へん · The number of times something happens, actions, deeds, experiences, etc.
犬[いぬ]を １[いっ]匹[ぴき]と 猫[ねこ]を ２[に]匹[ひき] 飼[か]っています。

匹 · ひき · Small or medium-sized animals.

Emotion
渋谷[しぶや]へは どこで 乗[の]り換[か]えるんですか？
Where do I transfer to go to Shibuya?
Travel

"渋谷へ" refers to the destination "Shibuya," with "へ" indicating the direction or destination. "は" is the topic particle, marking Shibuya as the topic of the sentence. "どこで" means "where" in the context of a location or action, and "乗り換える" (nori kaeru) means "to transfer" or "to change trains." "んですか" is a polite way to ask for an explanation or information, often used to seek clarification.
パン屋[や]さんで 食[しょく] パン １[いち]斤[きん] 買[か]ってきて。

I want to be someone who takes on a role in Tofugu.
Counter,Somewhat Common
翼 · よく · Wings, or to count birds in a more poetic way. Roles, spots, or posts.
この カプセルを 寝[ね]る 前[まえ]に 2[に] 錠[じょう] 飲[の]んでください。
Please take two capsules before bed.

錠 · じょう · Pills and tablets. Supplements that aren't considered medicine are normally counted using 粒 (つぶ) instead.

一緒[いっしょ]に 写真[しゃしん]を 撮[と]ってください
Please take a picture with me.
Travel
一緒に (issho ni) means "together," 写真 (shashin) means "photo," 撮って (totte) is "take" in the te-form, and ください (kudasai) is a polite request.
抽選[ちゅうせん]で 米俵[こめだわら] 3[さん]俵[ひょう]が 当[あ]たった。
I won two straw sacks of rice from the raffle.
Counter,Somewhat Common
俵 · ひょう · Straw bags or sacks of rice, salt, etc.
請求[せいきゅう]書[しょ]に 間違[まちが]いが ある ようですが
It seems there is a mistake in the bill
Travel
請求書 (せいきゅうしょ, seikyūsho) means "bill" or "invoice," 間違い (まちがい, machigai) means "mistake," and あるようですが (aru yō desu ga) indicates a suggestion or observation, meaning "it seems."

尾 · び · Fish, and crustaceans with fins or tails.
仕上[しあ]げに 塩[しお]を 1[いち] 摘[つ]み入[い]れてください。

摘み · つまみ · Pinches of something.

塊 · かたまり · Balls, masses, lumps or chunks of meat, clouds, people, dirt, cheese, fish, etc.
その お芝居[しばい]は、 3[さん] 幕[まく]で 構成[こうせい] されていた。
That play was made up of three acts.
Counter,Somewhat Common
幕 · まく · Acts of a play or performance, memorable moments from real life.

I participated in a five-boat race.
Counter,Somewhat Common
艇 · てい · Boats, yachts, and sailing boats specifically made for and used in races.
この 約款[やっかん]には １２８[ひゃくにじゅうはち] 項[こう]もの 条項[じょうこう]が 書[か]かれていた。
This article had a hundred and twenty-eight clauses.
Counter,Somewhat Common
項 · こう · Clauses in an article or legal document.
盗難[とうなん] 証明[しょうめい]書[しょ] 作[つく]ってください
Please make a theft report.
Travel
盗難証明書 (とうなんしょうめいしょ, tōnan shōmei-sho) means "theft report," and 作ってください (つくってください, tsukutte kudasai) means "please make."
１[いち] 欠片[けっぺん]の 勇気[ゆうき]を 振[ふ]り絞[しぼ]った。
I mustered up a slice of courage.
Counter,Somewhat Common
欠片 · かけら · Pieces of something, shards of glass, slices of bread, garlic cloves, pieces of ginger, pieces of anything, etc.
風呂[ふろ]は 何時[なんどき]まで 利用[りよう] できますか？
Until what time can I use the bath?
鼠,Travel
１[いっ]週間[しゅうかん] ずっと 風邪[かぜ]で 寝込[ねこ]んでいた。
I had a cold and was in bed all week.
Counter,Common

週 · しゅう · 週 is used to count weeks. Most of the time, you'll want to add the suffix 間 (かん) which changes "week" to "for __ weeks.". If you add the ordinal number suffix 目 to 週 it identifies which week you're talking about. ３週目 means "the third week," and １週目 means "the first week." Alternatively, you could add the ordinal number prefix 第 (だい). 第１週 would mean "the first week" as well.
あなたの ために 一生[いっしょう] 懸命[けんめい]、 頑張[がんば]る。
I'll try my best for you.
Emotion
落雷[らくらい]で 電波[でんぱ] 塔[とう]が 3[さん] 塔[とう] 倒[たお]れてしまった。
Three radio towers fell due to the lightning.
Counter,Somewhat Common
塔 · とう · Towers, steeples, tall monuments, pagodas, stupas, etc.
5[ご] 班[はん]に 別[わか]れて 教室[きょうしつ]の 掃除[そうじ]を しました。
We were divided into five groups, and we cleaned the classroom.
Counter,Somewhat Common
班 · はん · Groups and squads.
被災[ひさい] 地[ち]に テント 65[ろくじゅうご]張[ば]りが 設置[せっち] された。
Sixty-five tents have been set up at the disaster area.
Counter,Somewhat Common
張/張り · はり · Things that can be spread out. This includes tents, mosquito nets, and stage curtains.
一[いち]日[にち] 32[さんじゅうに] 品目[ひんもく] 摂[と]る ように 心[こころ]がけています。
I'm trying to ingest thirty-two different ingredients per day.
Counter,Somewhat Common

品目 · ひんもく · Items, types of products, varieties of dishes, meals, and types or numbers of ingredients. Be careful not to mix up 品目 with the counter 品 attached to the ordinal number suffix 目 (しなめ). If you see 四品目はラーメン and it means "the fourth dish is ramen," it's よんしなめ. However, if it means "ramen with four ingredients," it's よんひんもく. The reading is entirely dependent on the context, so try to pay close attention when using these two counters.
この 小説[しょうせつ]の 第[だい]3[さん]版[ばん]は、 既[すで]に 第[だい]5[ご]刷[さつ]も 刷[す]られている。
The third edition of this novel is in its fifth printing already.
Counter,Somewhat Common
刷/刷り · すり · Printings, pressings, impressions. If you want to count the number of copies made of a specific printing, use 部 (ぶ).
帰[かえ]りに お豆腐[とうふ]屋[や]さんで お豆腐[とうふ] 1[いち]丁[ちょう]を 買[か]って 帰[かえ]ってきて。
Can you buy a block of tofu at the tofu store on your way back?
Counter,Somewhat Common
丁 · ちょう · Tofu, koyadofu, ganmodoki, hanpen, konnyaku, tuna, orders of ramen, orders of soba, lively actions, games, matches, kitchen knives, scissors, etc.
トーフグは ポートランドで 豆腐[とうふ]屋[や]を 5[ご]店[てん] 経営[けいえい] している。
Tofugu is running five tofu shops in Portland.
Counter,Somewhat Common
店 · てん · Shops, restaurants, and branches or chains of companies. You can also use two other counters, 軒 (けん) and 店舗 (てんぽ), for shops and restaurants, but 軒 is not used for branches.
この 写真[しゃしん]は、 ２００万[にれいれいまん] 画素[がそ]の コンデジで 撮[と]った ものです。
I took this photo with a 2,000,000 pixel compact digital camera.
Counter,Somewhat Common
画素 · がそ · Pixels.
1[いち] 説[せつ]に よると、 コウイチは 豆腐[とうふ]も 河豚[ふぐ]も 食[た]べられない そうだよ。
According to one rumor, Koichi can eat neither tofu nor fugu.
Counter,Somewhat Common
説 · せつ · Views, theories, and rumors.
火事[かじ]で 家屋[かおく]が 7[なな]棟[むね] 全焼[ぜんしょう] した。
Seven houses were completely burned down by the fire.
Counter,Somewhat Common

棟 · とう/むね · Buildings and houses. It's also used to count buildings that humans do not live in, like garages, detached storehouses, and sheds. The kanji can be read either as とう or むね, but they're both about equally common. When the reading is とう, it uses the kango readings. When the reading is むね, one and two are wago and the rest are kango.
伏見[ふしみ] 稲荷[いなり] 大社[たいしゃ]は ここから 遠[とお]いですか？
Is Fushimi Inari Shrine far from here?
Travel
伏見稲荷大社 (ふしみいなりたいしゃ, Fushimi Inari Taisha) is the proper noun for the shrine.
東京[とうきょう] 大学[だいがく]を 目指[めざ]して 3[さん]浪[ろう] しています。
I've been studying for Tokyo University for the last three years (since failing the first time).
Counter,Somewhat Common
浪 · ろう · Number of years a person has been studying to pass college or university entrance exams—but only after they failed the first time.
嵐[あらし]で、 この 町[まち]の 電話[でんわ] 回線[かいせん]が ４[よん] 回線[かいせん] 壊[こわ]れた。
Because of the storm, four phone lines got broken in this town.
Counter,Somewhat Common
回線 · かいせん · Electrical circuit or phone/Internet lines, as well as their connections.
昨日[きのう] 桜[さくら]を 見[み]に 行[い]ったけど まだ 5[ご]分[ふん] 咲[さ]きでした。
I went to see the cherry blossoms yesterday, but they were still only half-bloomed.
Counter,Somewhat Common

分 · ぶ · Ten percent units as well as degrees. It's a unit of body temperature (one-tenth or one degree), one percent of a bank rate or interest rate, a traditional Japanese unit of length of about 0.303cm (one-tenth of 寸/すん), tabi socks or shoes of 0.21cm (one-tenth of 1文 もん), a traditional Japanese weight unit of 0.375g (one-tenth of 1匁/もんめ), and a unit of Edo period money (one-fourth of gold 1両/りょう or one-tenth of silver 1匁/もんめ).
その 海賊[かいぞく]は、 悪魔[あくま]を １[いち]刺[さ]しで 死[し]に 追[お]いやった。
That pirate put the demon down with a single thrust.
Counter,Somewhat Common
刺し · さし · Stabs—whether whatever is getting stabbed is being stung by bees, pierced with spears, or happens to be bites of food spiked onto skewers.
台風[たいふう]の 影響[えいきょう]で 4[よん] 路線[ろせん]の ダイヤが 乱[みだ]れております。
Train services on four lines are not running on schedule due to the typhoon.
Counter,Somewhat Common
路線 · ろせん · Train lines, bus routes.
トーフグの 社員[しゃいん]は 2[に]派[は]に 分裂[ぶんれつ] して 対立[たいりつ] している。
The Tofugu employees split up into two factions and are fighting each other.
Counter,Somewhat Common
派 · は · Groups, parties, schools, factions, denominations, and sects.
今年[ことし]は 真珠[しんじゅ]の 3[さん]連[れん] ネックレスが 流行[はや]ってるらしいよ。
Apparently three-strand pearl necklaces are trendy this year.
Counter,Somewhat Common
連 · れん · Similarly-shaped items strung together or in rows—for example, a string of pearls or prayer beads. More recently, it's been used to count shots taken in gacha games.
この 店[みせ]は、 東京[とうきょう]で 22[にじゅうに] 店舗[てんぽ] 展開[てんかい] する ドーナツ屋[や] チェーンです。
This shop is a donut chain that has twenty-two locations in Tokyo.
Counter,Somewhat Common
店舗 · てんぽ · Shops, restaurants, and branches or chains of companies. You can use two other Japanese counters, 店 (てん) and 軒 (けん), for shops and restaurants, but 軒 is not used for branches.
明日[あした]は ３[さん] コマ 講義[こうぎ]を しなくては いけないから、 準備[じゅんび]で 忙[いそが]しい。
I have to do three lectures tomorrow, so I'm busy with my prep.
Counter,Somewhat Common
齣 · こも · Scenes of a play/movie/drama, classes, lessons, lectures, etc. The 齣 counter is usually written in katakana as コマ.
歌舞伎[かぶき]の 公演[こうえん]は 何時[いつ]に 始[はじ]まりますか？
What time does the kabuki performance start?
Travel
歌舞伎 (かぶき, kabuki) refers to the traditional theater, 公演 (こうえん, kōen) means "performance," and 始まる (はじまる, hajimaru) means "to begin."
４００[よんひゃく] 字[じ]詰[づ]め 原稿[げんこう]用[よう]紙[し]を １００[ひゃく]枚[まい] 買[か]ってきて！
Can you go buy a hundred sheets of four-hundred-character manuscript paper?
Counter,Somewhat Common
字 · じ · Letters, characters.

Counter,Somewhat Common

なくす (nakusu) means "to lose," and してしまいました (shite shimaimashita) implies the action was completed, often with a sense of regret.
あなたが すごく 羨[うらや]ましいなぁ。

憂鬱[ゆううつ]だ。

Emotion

壊れる (こわれる, kowareru) means "to break," and ています (teimasu) indicates a continuous or resulting state.
もう 誰[だれ]も 愛[あい]せない。

誰[だれ]に 聞[き]けばいいですか？

誰 (だれ, dare) means "who," and 聞けばいいですか (きけばいいですか, kikeba ii desu ka) means "should I ask?"
誰[だれ]に そんな 口[くち]を きいてる！？

Emotion
あなたは 誰[だれ]とも 比[くら]べられない。
Nobody can compare to you.
Emotion
誰[だれ]よりも あなたに 近[ちか]くなりたい。

Emotion
この ピアノ、 ３[さん] 鍵[かぎ] 壊[こわ]れてるんだよね。

Counter,Somewhat Common

みかん １[いち] 籠[かご] ２９８[にひゃくきゅうじゅうはち]円[えん]なの？ じゃあ、 ３[さん] 籠[かご] ください。

Counter,Somewhat Common
籠 · かご · Baskets and/or piles of whatever is inside a basket.
大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です
It's okay / It's fine./I'm okay
Travel

大丈夫 (daijōbu) means "okay," "alright," or "fine." It can be used to express that something is not a problem or that you're not in need of assistance. です (desu) is a polite ending that makes the statement more formal. This phrase is often used to reassure someone that everything is fine or to decline help politely.
